data.name: Hadassina
data.gender_notes: Hadassina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Hadassah means myrtle tree. Myrtle was a symbol of royalty and beauty in ancient Israel. The prophet Isaiah wrote, 'The Lord will create over all the earth one new man, and they shall all dwell safely. And a new moon shall be great over the house of David, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall rejoice, and give gladness, and joy, and corn, and wine, and oil, and milk, and honey, and a soul shall be saved, for the seed of Judah, and a child shall be born for this city; and the days of her mourning shall be ended, because the desolation is departed from her, and she shall be called Myrtle Tree, and the place thereof Shame out of the Lord; for the Lord hath chosen Zion, and will sanctify it; this shall be her name for evermore.', which refers to the rebirth and restoration of Jerusalem, represented by the myrtle tree.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the beauty, joy, and hope that comes with new beginnings.
data.etymology: Hadassina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Myrtle flower.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hadassina total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: הדסינה
in_hebrew.meaning: עץ הדס, סמל של חברות ואהבה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם הדסינה מקורו בעברית ומייצג את העץ הדס, שהיה סמל של חברות ואהבה. בבית המקדש, הדסים היו ניטעים באזור הכותל המערבי. העץ גם ייצג את אהבת האלוהים, כפי שהוזכר בספר שיר השירים (1:14).

in_greek.name: Χαδασσίνα
in_greek.meaning: βλάστημα του δαφνός, σύμβολο της αγάπης
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χαδασσίνα προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για τη δάφνη, με τη δάφνη να συμβολίζει την αγάπη. Στον Ιουδαϊσμό, η δάφνη ήταν ένα σύμβολο της αιώνιας αγάπης του Θεού. Στον Χριστιανισμό, η δάφνη απεικονίζει την αγάπη και την ειλικρίνεια, όπως αναφέρεται στο Ευαγγέλιο του Λουκά (10:27).

in_latin.name: Hadassina
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Hadassina a radice Hebraica derivatur, significans flos carni, id est caritas. In Ecclesia primitiva, flos carni erat symbolus amoris, quem Deus habet erga hominem. In traditione Christiana, flos carni repraesentat dilectio et sinceritas, ut in Evangelio secundum Lucam (10,27) scriptum est.

in_english.name: Hadassina
in_english.meaning: myrtle flower, symbol of love and friendship
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hadassina originates from the Hebrew roots, meaning myrtle flower, symbol of love and friendship. In the Bible, myrtle is mentioned in the book of Isaiah (41:19) and is associated with Israel's restoration. In the Christian tradition, the myrtle flower represents love, friendship, and devotion, as seen in the book of Proverbs (31:10).

data.cultural_impact: The name Hadassina, derived from Hadassah, can evoke a sense of beauty, strength, and royalty, as myrtle trees were highly valued in ancient Israel for their aesthetic appeal and their ability to provide essential resources such as food and wood. The name can also represent a connection to the rich history and cultural heritage of the Jewish people.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hadassina can be seen as a reminder of God's promise to restore and renew His people, as represented by the myrtle tree in Isaiah 43. It can also serve as a symbol of faithfulness, as myrtle trees are known for their long-lasting and enduring nature. Additionally, the name can be a source of comfort and hope, as it points towards the ultimate restoration and redemption of God's creation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hadassah, a biblical name meaning my breast, represents nourishment and the sustaining love of God. In the Old Testament, Hadassah is better known as Esther, a queen who saved her people from destruction through her wisdom and courage. Thus, Hadassina signifies strength and provision in times of need.

historical_references.reference: Hadassah, a beautiful Jewish woman, was saved from King Xerxes' decree to annihilate all the Jews in Shushan. She was taken to the harem of the king, renamed Esther, and eventually saved her people by revealing her Jewish identity to the king and exposing the plot of Haman to destroy them.

Hadassah, a prophetess, played a significant role in the early Christian community. She was known for her wisdom and prophecies. According to tradition, she lived around the time of Christ and was instrumental in the conversion of the Roman centurion Longinus to Christianity.
